purpose: Realistic prompts for independent skill evaluation; expected notes are withheld from the answering agent.

cases.prompt: Our invoices already have validated ISO due dates and payment dates. Should we use a decision model to decide whether each payment was late?
cases.expected: Keep date comparison exact; handle timezone/business policy explicitly; do not add inference for its own sake.

cases.prompt: We generate JSON with a large LLM to sort refund emails, then a service issues refunds when confidence is above 0.9. Audit this design. Emails may omit order IDs.
cases.expected: Separate intent from eligibility/authority; unknown evidence and fallback; typed classifier insertion with held-out cost/coverage and no copied threshold.

cases.prompt: Our community library has funding for three of eight proposed programs. Staff notes describe likely demand and accessibility, and costs are known. Help us make the decision.
cases.expected: MCDA/expected utility for bounded evidence; explicit human values/weights and budget solver or enumeration; uncertainty/VOI and sensitivity; no vendor-forced software redesign.

cases.prompt: Our passage reranker emits a score of 0.92. Can we treat that as 92 percent probability a claim is true and publish automatically?
cases.expected: Distinguish relevance score and claim truth; inspect score semantics and matched evaluation; evidence sufficiency/contradiction; policy owns publishing.

cases.prompt: Four model checks each pass 95 percent of the time. They share the same document. Is the chance all four are right 0.95 to the fourth?
cases.expected: No independence assumption from parallel/shared state; marginals versus joints and outcome evaluation, dependence-aware bounds if appropriate.

cases.prompt: I calibrated a 90 percent conformal prediction set on last month's tickets. Can every singleton result bypass review for this month's new language and enterprise customers?
cases.expected: Marginal coverage under assumptions; shift and subgroup limitation; singleton not permission; evaluate conditional selective risk and revalidate.

cases.prompt: A classifier must pick sales, billing, or technical support. It assigns an unsubscribe request to billing with confidence 1.0. Raising the threshold did not help. Fix the design.
cases.expected: Candidate coverage, no-match plus missing/conflicting evidence if needed; test true label removed/unknown; high confidence cannot recover absent answer.

cases.prompt: We wrote an Alloy model of access control and a decision model says it looks safe. Can we skip exploring counterexamples and use that as our security acceptance?
cases.expected: Judgment as triage only; checker scope/model validity/non-vacuous properties; execution authorization exact; actual evidence required.

cases.prompt: Our model predicts which suppliers will deliver late. Should we fine them to make delivery faster? We have only historical order data, and managers intervened on the highest-risk orders.
cases.expected: Prediction versus causal intervention; confounding/selection; define utility, ethics/authority and controlled or identified causal evaluation; no action benefit inferred from prediction.

cases.prompt: A local constrained decoder has the same JSON API as Jev and agrees on 95 of 100 examples, twice as fast. Is it a drop-in replacement for our approval queue?
cases.expected: Contract compatibility versus semantics/calibration/runtime performance; paired action-level error/coverage/cost and representative labels, uncertainty; no broad parity claim.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this sentence more clearly: The meeting was moved because the room was unavailable.
cases.expected: Non-trigger control: simply rewrite, no Augustus process or decision card.

cases.prompt: A repo we catalogued has 200 more stars, a new SHA, and an updated README that retracts a calibration result. How should Augustus absorb this update?
cases.expected: Same identity revisit, inspect actual claim change and retain retraction provenance; archive popularity; targeted conceptual update only if changed decision; no replicated locks.

cases.prompt: We replaced the official client with a compatible wrapper. It averages option permutations and puts the winning mean probability in confidence. Can our existing confidence >= 0.8 approval rule stay unchanged?
cases.expected: Schema compatibility does not preserve statistic semantics; version wrapper/aggregation, recalibrate and evaluate paired action risk/coverage, preserve authority and hold rollout pending evidence.

cases.prompt: Two orderings assign the true label probabilities 0.8 and 0.4. Averaging gives 0.6. A teammate says Jensen proves this beats either ordering and is calibrated, so eight sampled permutations make any Choice safe. Check that claim and propose the smallest test.
cases.expected: Jensen bounds average convex loss, not best member, accuracy, calibration or action safety; label alignment, full versus sampled/canonical frozen construction, random provider effects and measured overhead; held-out paired test.

cases.prompt: A multimodal decision head supports video and returns high confidence that a 10-minute inspection contains no fault. Its loader samples 16 frames. Can we let it sign off the inspection?
cases.expected: Observed media coverage versus full temporal claim; missed-event counterexample, frame/window provenance and per-modality validation; narrow baseline or collect adequate evidence; no score-based signoff authority.

cases.prompt: Our RAG filter keeps 15 percent of chunks and the model judge accepts 98 of 100 answers in both arms. The timer starts after filtering and the cost chart uses another model's token rate. Can we announce equal quality at lower cost?
cases.expected: Not equivalence from matching small-sample judge totals; paired labels/uncertainty and margin, evidence recall, own pipeline rates/cache/retries, full timing boundary and unknown costs; separate proxy estimate from measured claim.

cases.prompt: Our frozen routing rule made no mistakes on 20 independent accepted examples in a rare category. Can we claim its error is below 1 percent with 95 percent confidence? We also have 40 other categories.
cases.expected: No; one-sided zero-error upper bound about 13.9 percent; 299 needed for one fixed category with zero errors under IID assumptions, more or appropriate correction for simultaneous categories; no search on certification sample; retain review or gather support.

cases.prompt: Appending hostile text changed 12 of 20 classifier answers. We repeated each case five times and want to publish a 60 percent injection vulnerability rate over 100 independent samples. Is that a sound claim?
cases.expected: Need clean and matched harmless controls, invariant/adjudicated labels and eligible denominators; repeated cases clustered not independent; bounded authored suite not population estimate; preserve host authority.

cases.prompt: A positive scalar temperature calibration leaves every top label unchanged. Does this prove the approval workflow is unchanged when it uses a probability threshold?
cases.expected: Argmax invariance does not preserve threshold actions; concrete crossing example, calibrator/policy versioning and held-out action-level requalification.

cases.prompt: Our frozen classifier abstains using an uncalibrated margin score. We evaluated its accepted-case error and coverage on an untouched representative holdout. A reviewer says selective classification is invalid until the margin becomes a calibrated probability. Is that necessarily true?
cases.expected: No universal calibration prerequisite for ranking/selection; require adequate valid risk/coverage evaluation and distinguish probability-derived policy, statistical guarantee, empirical result and deployment shift.

cases.prompt: Our tool issues a payment, then an exact monitor checks authorization and stops the next action if the payment was unauthorized. Have we guaranteed that unauthorized payments cannot occur?
cases.expected: Post-action detection cannot prevent first irreversible violation; authorize exact target/value before effect atomically, fallback/timing/recoverability assumptions, retain outcome reconciliation separately.

cases.prompt: Our hosted classifier gives a useful probability vector, and our policy computes expected loss from it. Must we train a specialist just because we consume the distribution rather than the winning label?
cases.expected: No; choose by measured performance, constraints and maintenance economics; qualify probability semantics and calibration/policy against independent outcomes on either surface.

cases.prompt: Our retrieval-to-answer baseline already meets our prespecified quality, evidence-recall, latency and cost targets. Do we have to add an absolute keep/no-match classifier before generation because ranking alone is not relevance probability?
cases.expected: No forced gate; ranking not absolute adequacy but baseline can suffice; add only when task policy requires distinction and controlled evaluation justifies it; retrieval recall and failure fallback still matter.

cases.prompt: A fair coin and a supplier case with no evidence both produce Noul 0.5. Does that number alone tell us whether we should gather more information?
cases.expected: Equal binary assignment/max Bernoulli entropy does not diagnose uncertainty or VOI; distinguish reducible missing evidence from known inherent variability and decision cost/observation model.

cases.prompt: Alloy 6 completed an assertion check using NuSMV and an unbounded temporal horizon, within a fixed finite signature scope. Is this only evidence about the first ten steps? Is it proof for arbitrary object counts or our production code?
cases.expected: Complete temporal checking covers all modeled traces within that finite object scope when completed; not merely default bounded horizon, not arbitrary populations or deployed implementation; record exact configuration/model/property and adequacy checks.

cases.prompt: Can a distilled student ever correct a teacher's mistakes without independent gold labels during training, or must it reproduce every teacher error?
cases.expected: Can improve via aggregation, regularization or student inductive bias; no universal error reproduction or improvement; teacher agreement not truth, independent outcome evaluation needed.

cases.prompt: A decision model improves our independently measured outcome quality at slightly higher latency, still within our hard SLA and budget. Must we reject it because it does not beat the simpler baseline on quality, latency and cost simultaneously?
cases.expected: No Pareto dominance requirement; explicit prespecified utility and hard constraints, full cost/uncertainty and acceptable tradeoff, reject only if targets/utility unsupported.

cases.prompt: Our second-stage classifier has 5 percent error on all tickets. A new first-stage gate sends it only difficult tickets, 20 percent of traffic. Can we budget system errors as 0.2 times 0.05 and keep its old calibration?
cases.expected: Use downstream conditional error on selected population and complete branches; old marginal qualification does not transfer, no independence or free recalibration guarantee; measure selection and fallback outcomes.

cases.prompt: Y and C are independent fair bits. Signal A=C and signal B=Y XOR C each tell us nothing about Y alone. Our downstream program already knows C. Are A and B interchangeable components? What does this teach us about replacing decision models?
cases.expected: B plus C recovers Y while A adds nothing; compare relevant joint or conditional information and policy outcomes rather than isolated accuracy or information order; learned context and versions matter.

cases.prompt: We improved a refund-routing prompt through 80 rounds on the same 200 eval tickets. The model-judge score is up 12 points. Each round had a 95 percent confidence interval. Build the next evaluation and promotion plan, including what to implement and what to keep fixed.
cases.expected: Search evidence not independent confirmation, optional stopping/multiplicity/adaptive reuse; independent labels/outcomes and frozen candidate, complete episode loss/authority constraints, meaningful baseline, heldout plan/run artifacts budget regression/rollback; no claimed empirical gain from proxy.

cases.prompt: A blog says entropy minimization and a thermodynamic free-energy analogy prove that an ensemble of decision models will improve every agent workflow. Should Augustus promote this into its core calculus? If not, how could we still develop a useful method from it?
cases.expected: Reject universal claim and metaphor-as-proof; map event distributions, variables/units/objective/assumptions, best conditional method and counterexample, compare full-outcome baseline at equal budget; no source-popularity synthesis.

cases.prompt: Our frozen hosted classifier returns probabilities over five intents. We send a case to a human reviewer when its Shannon entropy is above a threshold and auto-approve the rest. We describe this as softmax-response selective classification adapted to that reviewer, and we report only the error rate on auto-approved cases. Are the description and the report right?
cases.expected: No on both. Beyond two options entropy and top-label mass can order cases differently, so an entropy band is not softmax response, and neither score is by itself P(correct). A frozen head's band is not adapted to the reviewer; that needs the reviewer's measured outcomes (a rejector or per-case handler loss). Auto-approved error omits the reviewer's errors, delay and load on the deferred slice. Compare the rule with a top-mass cut, always-approve and always-defer on held-out system loss; policy, not the score, authorizes auto-approval.

cases.prompt: Our fraud model sends uncertain card disputes to one analyst team that can review 300 cases a day. At our chosen threshold it would defer about 900 a day. The analysts are right 97 percent of the time on a random sample of disputes. Can we keep the threshold and count every deferred case as 97 percent accurate?
cases.expected: No. Deferral is an action with a handler, queue, delay and cost: 900 exceeds 300, so the policy must fit capacity or name and count the overflow outcome (backlog delay, a default action, or ranking by expected loss). Accuracy on random disputes does not transfer to the harder deferred slice or an overloaded team, and it depends on what analysts are shown; measure reviewer accuracy and queue delay on deferred cases as deployed. Compare total system loss with feasible baselines; policy owns the threshold.

cases.prompt: Our retriever sometimes returns a single candidate product. We still ask the hosted decision model to choose among the candidates and auto-apply when its confidence is at least 0.9. Anything wrong with that?
cases.expected: Yes. With one option the concentration statistic is 1.0 by construction, so confidence compares nothing and the gate always fires. Branch on candidate count in code: a closed singleton resolves in code without a model call; open coverage needs a none/other option or a separate fit judgment. Test retrieval misses separately; policy owns auto-apply.

cases.prompt: Since launch we estimate the error rate of our auto-approval policy from the cases our reviewers happen to see plus customer complaints. Traffic is growing, so the estimate should keep getting better, right?
cases.expected: No. Review queues and complaints are selected samples; bias does not shrink with more traffic, and auto-approved or unreviewed cases may be unobserved. Estimate error from outcomes on every case or a known-probability audit sample that includes auto-approved cases, weighted by inverse inclusion probability. Label provenance and review display still matter. A deterministic outcome available on every case removes the need for an audit sample.

cases.prompt: Our coding agent marks a task done when the test suite passes and it has written a success log. The agent can edit any file in the repository, including the tests. Is that a sound completion check?
cases.expected: No. A deterministic check is not independent if the judged agent can write what it reads: edited tests and self-written logs can be forged. Verify against evidence the agent cannot forge (protected or CI-owned tests, diffs of test changes, host or server state, signed receipts), keep the done-judgment advisory, and test the check with a red-team case that edits tests. Policy, not the agent's report, closes the task.

cases.prompt: Compute 17% of 2,340.
cases.expected: Non-trigger control: answer 397.8 directly; no Augustus process or decision card.

cases.prompt: Install the TypeSafe SDK in this repo and wire my API key from .env.
cases.expected: Non-trigger control: provider setup alone. No decision card; follow the provider's current docs instead of inventing package names or commands, and keep the key out of code, logs and commits.

cases.prompt: We want a small local classifier to replace our Jev calls. Plan to label last quarter's tickets with Jev Choice outputs and distill them into a fine-tuned encoder, then switch over.
cases.expected: Check the provider's terms before any Jev output enters training: TypeSafe's customer agreement bars using Jev Output for distillation or imitation training, so use independent labels, observed outcomes, code-computed labels, or a teacher whose terms allow it. Keep Jev only as a separately stored comparator if at all. Consider whether to train at all; compare against the incumbent on held-out real outcomes with a rollback plan.

cases.prompt: Help me train a local support-intent classifier from our application's CSV export. It has 18,000 rows: individual replies from the same ticket, quoted copies, customer IDs, final queue, and resolution notes written after routing. Some billing tickets end up with engineering; two reviewers disagree about the right queue. We want to route the first incoming message for new customers next month. How should we turn this into a usable training and evaluation set?
cases.expected: Define the prediction-time input and intended label rather than treating final queue as truth. Exclude future resolution information, reconcile or explicitly retain ambiguous/multilabel/unknown cases with label provenance, and account for quoted duplicates and ticket/customer dependence. Split to match new-customer future use, keeping related records out of opposing folds; fit preprocessing only on training data. Inspect missingness and class support and reserve independent confirmation before tuning. Do not report achieved performance from a data plan.

cases.prompt: Choose a starting model and training method for our six-intent on-device helpdesk router. We have 700 independently labeled short messages, no GPU, no network at inference, a 150 MB artifact limit, and a 40 ms p95 target on our office laptops. A colleague wants us to do prompt tuning, then adapters, then full fine-tuning in that order. What would you actually try within two CPU-hours, and what evidence would change your choice?
cases.expected: Choose a feasible small comparison based on language coverage, usable stock/license, hardware and measured end-to-end limits; a sparse linear model or compact frozen encoder plus head can be a reasonable start, not a mandatory answer. Methods are alternatives conditional on constraints, not a universal progression. Specify a bounded run and independent task-quality comparison with the incumbent; measure size/latency on the target and retain uncertainty. Do not assume every base supports every method or promise unmeasured SLA compliance.

cases.prompt: We're training a warranty escalation model. Missing a truly urgent claim costs 200 units; escalating a routine one costs 5; correct decisions cost zero. The binary model gives an urgent probability of 0.08. My teammate proposes a 0.5 cutoff, then the same cutoff on max softmax when we add routine, urgent, and fraud classes. Next quarter entirely new claim types will arrive. Help us design and test the decision layer without letting it approve payouts.
cases.expected: For valid binary posterior semantics, escalation costs 4.6 and routine handling 16 at 0.08; escalation is preferable and the equal-loss threshold is 5/205, not 0.5. Qualify probability estimates on representative independent outcomes rather than applying cost math to arbitrary scores. Multiclass needs action-by-class losses and expected loss per action; max softmax alone neither specifies action utility nor detects absent classes. Specify unknown/abstain handling and held-out unseen-type tests, preserving payout authority outside the model. Do not force a binary threshold formula onto multiclass or open-set decisions.

cases.prompt: I can afford four CPU-hours to improve our local ticket classifier. We have a training set, a development set we have already used to choose features, and a sealed sample from a later month with disjoint customer groups and independently adjudicated labels. Set up a small adaptive search over preprocessing, head choice, and hyperparameters. If the sealed sample disappoints, can we use its mistakes to choose another candidate and still call it our final test?
cases.expected: Bound trials, wall time and stopping, track seeds/configurations, retain failed trials and a feasible incumbent, and compare on development data with group boundaries intact. Freeze preprocessing/model/policy and acceptance criteria before independent confirmation. A sample inspected to select a replacement becomes development evidence; obtain a fresh independent confirmation set or explicitly limit the claim. Do not label repeated search gains or merely planned runs as confirmed improvement; budget exhaustion or no worthwhile gain may retain the incumbent.

cases.prompt: I asked for a trained model to route renewal notices, but the export contains an authoritative notice_type enum and operations has an approved routing table for every supported value. Last month's mistakes were all stale entries in the deployed copy; new values must go to operations for review. We have only 30 hand-labeled free-text notes. What should we ship this week?
cases.expected: Prefer fixing/versioning the exact mapping and unknown-value fallback with tests over training on scarce incidental notes. Preserve review for new enums and monitor real routing outcomes; do not train a ceremonial baseline or require more labels before making the exact fix. State when an actual semantic ambiguity would justify revisiting training, without inventing one here.

cases.prompt: Our local three-class classifier works in the training notebook. Please plan the release checks for exporting it to our service's Choice-shaped JSON API. The exported runtime may reorder labels, and our adapter currently writes the largest raw logit into confidence. The service uses confidence to skip human review. What must survive a fresh-process reload, and is matching the hosted API's field names enough?
cases.expected: Check reloaded preprocessing/tokenizer, label order, weights, calibrator and policy/config versions against fixed representative inputs, including asymmetric logits, ties, invalid input and abstention. Compare actual outputs/actions within justified numeric tolerances and fail release on label swaps or changed review decisions. Raw logits are not probabilities or Jev concentration; softmax normalization alone does not establish calibration or hosted semantic parity. Explicitly version adapter semantics and qualify the policy independently; include dependencies and artifact identity for reproducibility. A prose checklist is not evidence export/reload was executed.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this release-note sentence in plain English: The classifier training job now serializes the tokenizer alongside the exported weights.
cases.expected: Non-trigger control: rewrite the sentence directly without starting model training, evaluation planning, or a trainer workflow. Training terminology inside copy-editing is not a training request.
